name: Youth of Today
label: Revelation
lede: Two kids from a Danbury hardcore band drew a hard line, put an X on it, and taught a whole generation of New York hardcore to wear varsity jackets, skip the beer and the burger, and mean every word.

eras.title: Out of Violent Children
eras.text: Ray Cappo and John Porcelly had already cut their teeth in the Danbury, Connecticut band Violent Children. Their new group picked the plainest name it could find and pointed it straight at New York, with a sober, clean-living message no one had asked for yet.

years.h: Two Violent Children start over
years.p: Cappo on vocals, Porcell on guitar, Graham Phillips on bass and Darren Pesce on drums. The name had already turned up in songs by Cause for Alarm and Abused; Porcell says they wanted something generic so people knew they were there to play hardcore.

years.h: First show: the Anthrax, with a push from [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]]
years.p: The debut lands at the Connecticut club that was the region's hardcore clubhouse. Porcell credits Agnostic Front's [[Roger Miret|ab51d57f-5007-4ee4-8461-a4050f8d939d]] and [[Vinnie Stigma|ebc05559-b4e0-4080-87d7-1c6672451491]] with getting them the gig.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ray Cappo · Revelation Records bio · Wikipedia: Revelation Records
years.h: Can't Close My Eyes 7" · Positive Force No. 4
years.p: [[Kevin Seconds|dfa1dec9-a570-4a1c-a2bb-0f07f6dbb81b]] of 7 Seconds puts it out on his Reno label, the straight edge stamp of approval before anyone in New York had heard of them. The same year the band turns up on the Connecticut Fun compilation LP.
years.xp:
Seconds was a direct influence on Cappo, and Positive Force was the obvious home: the label had built its name on positive, drug-free hardcore. Phillips and Pesce were gone soon after the record, the first of many exits.

The EP never really went away. Revelation later ran a limited fourth pressing, and in 1997 gave it a full reissue.

eras.title: A crew, a van, a mission
eras.text: The line-up spun like a revolving door, but the records and the road turned Youth of Today into the band every kid in a hooded sweatshirt wanted to be. By the end of 1987 there was a label built partly around them and a scene with a name: youth crew.

years.h: Enter Setari and Birkenhead
years.p: [[Craig Setari|3908d895-a1af-42a7-b86b-93a3074057ee]] comes over from [[Straight Ahead|1fd60d7c-dc35-44f5-9162-4113b6ca4a69]] on bass, and [[Richie Birkenhead|7a1a6273-c31b-4828-8e20-0d6ea66943aa]] makes it a two-guitar band. The drum stool keeps changing hands.

years.h: The drum stool turns into a carousel
years.p: Darren Pesce is out, and in the space of about a year Tommy Carroll, [[Drew Thomas|ebc66701-0d59-49c9-ae21-4937edb96a6a]] of [[Bold|b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa]] and even [[Kevin Seconds|dfa1dec9-a570-4a1c-a2bb-0f07f6dbb81b]] take turns behind the kit, per Wikipedia's line-up history. In 1987 Lukey Luke has a short run on bass before Schreifels takes it.

years.h: Break Down the Walls · Wishing Well Records
years.p: The first full-length, cut in two days according to Porcell, and released on the California label run out of the [[Uniform Choice|d514a452-7088-4d49-a03c-9e37d76d38ea]] camp. It becomes the blueprint: fast, chanted, and aimed at the kids in the room.

years.h: Revelation Records opens in New Haven
years.p: Jordan Cooper and Cappo start the label to put out one record, [[Warzone|496da466-68e9-4cbb-9e86-cbb57eda861a]]'s Lower East Side Crew 7". Cappo would step away from the business in 1988.

years.h: New York City Hardcore: Together 7" · Revelation
years.p: Rev's roll call of the new straight edge New York bands, and Youth of Today lead the line.

q: We thought straight edge was an important message.
years.h: Coast to coast behind Break Down the Walls
years.p: The five-piece: Cappo, Porcell, Birkenhead, [[Walter Schreifels|9f350578-acdd-480e-8273-5eaf88842f1c]] on bass and [[Mike Ferraro|edffc714-f0a2-4d6c-b4c0-dc31e713481c]] on drums. Ferraro met Cappo on the Bowery near St. Marks, learned the set at Giant Studios, and played his first show in Canada with 7 Seconds.
years.xp:
The tour was a rolling argument with the old punk world. In Detroit the locals threw deer meat on stage. In Chandler, Arizona, a Nazi skinhead gang called them out to fight behind a McDonald's, then never turned up.

It was also a conversion drive. Buffalo produced its own disciples in Zero Tolerance, and by their second trip through Southern California the straight edge kids were packing the room past capacity.

years.h: Birkenhead to [[Underdog|de38fbd3-7155-497a-bf3c-1a8db3091859]], Ferraro to the front of a new band
years.p: Birkenhead leaves to focus on Underdog. [[Sammy Siegler|869c662b-574c-46ac-acf6-3dc6f025fd5a]], a teenage drummer out of [[Side By Side|8dc812b1-d387-4c45-8173-f0d5bd0c318f]], takes over behind the kit.

eras.title: India and back
eras.text: The peak year of youth crew was nearly the year Youth of Today disappeared. Cappo walked away, went to India, came back, and the band made its heaviest, most pointed record: straight edge was the floor now, and vegetarianism was the new line.

years.big: The singer walks out to find God
years.src: Wikipedia: We're Not in This Alone · Wikipedia: Ray Cappo
years.h: Cappo goes to India. The band stops
years.p: A brief split, while Cappo travels to India chasing a growing interest in Krishna consciousness.
years.xp:
Krishna consciousness lined up with everything the band already preached: no drugs, no drink, no meat. For Cappo it was the next step, not a detour, and it would eventually shape everything he did after Youth of Today.

The pause didn't last. He came back with the band rebuilt around Schreifels on bass and Siegler on drums.

years.h: Rev picks up Break Down the Walls as REV 8
years.p: The label Cappo helped start reissues the debut LP, and the band appears on Rev's New York City Hardcore: The Way It Is compilation.

years.src: Wikipedia: We're Not in This Alone
years.h: We're Not in This Alone · Caroline Records
years.p: Recorded at Chung King House of Metal in New York and produced by Cappo and Porcell. It opens with Cappo announcing the band is back. Live Free started life as an unreleased Project X song.
years.xp:
No More goes after the meat industry, and its cheap video cut in slaughterhouse footage from PETA. It's the moment vegetarianism becomes part of the youth crew uniform.

Caroline's original mix came out muddy. Fans complained, and the label remixed and re-pressed with a REMIX sticker on the sleeve.

years.h: Porcell and Ferraro start [[Judge|3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e]]
years.p: The drummer from the 1987 tour becomes a singer, with Porcell writing the riffs. It begins as a side project.

eras.title: Out on a farewell
eras.text: The band took the message across Europe, including a Yugoslavia that barely had a hardcore circuit, then decided it had said what it had to say. The goodbye came on Revelation, and the members scattered into the bands that defined the next few years.

years.h: Twelve countries in one European run
years.p: Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Germany, Switzerland, Austria, Yugoslavia, Italy, France, Belgium, the Netherlands and England. A show at Amsterdam's Van Hall later surfaces as a live 7".

q: Straight edge kids were hated back then.
years.src: Wikipedia: Youth of Today · No Echo
years.h: The goodbye record: Youth of Today 7" · REV 17
years.p: Four songs recorded as a farewell for Revelation. Three of them also came out as the Disengage single. Then the band calls it a day.
years.xp:
The split has been read by some as the moment the second wave of straight edge started to fade. The bands that followed took the youth crew sound heavier and stranger.

Porcell had put it simply years later: the ideals mattered more than the rules.

years.h: Cappo forms [[Shelter|d5157104-76b1-4b8b-90c2-9ff994f940db]]
years.p: Krishna-core, openly devotional, and eventually joined by Porcell. Schreifels already has [[Gorilla Biscuits|0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762]] and is headed for [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]].

eras.title: The door never quite shuts
eras.text: Youth of Today never staged a big reunion so much as kept leaving the door open. Short runs of shows, a recovered master and a new generation of kids kept the name alive while Shelter carried on.

years.h: The last line-up plays again
years.p: A brief reunion of the We're Not in This Alone four.

years.h: Another short return, with Bold's bassist
years.p: Cappo, Porcell and Siegler play again with Tim Brooks of [[Bold|b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa]] on bass.

years.h: The muddy mix gets fixed
years.p: Cappo and Porcell win back the rights in 1996 and make a third, definitive mix of We're Not in This Alone for Revelation's 1997 reissue, with new artwork. Rev reissues Can't Close My Eyes the same year.

years.h: Europe, with [[Ken Olden|94959ed9-83ae-46e1-b23f-88939fad93e6]] on bass
years.p: Cappo, Porcell and Siegler tour Europe, with Olden from [[Battery|172d89ba-95ab-4e30-92a2-fe836ba0601e]] and [[Better Than a Thousand|9a5d50be-8dff-4f2f-8852-aa4eafb8f985]] filling in. American shows follow in 2004.

eras.title: Back for good
eras.text: The return that started in a small Swiss town in 2010 never ended. Youth of Today became a working band again, headlining for kids born long after the CBGB matinees, and by 2016 the late-'80s rhythm section was back.

years.h: The comeback opens in Lyss, Switzerland
years.p: A European tour with Olden on bass and Vinny Panza on drums. By the first week of December they're in Peru, Chile, Argentina and Brazil.

years.h: Moscow and Oslo
years.p: Two shows in Russia and two in Norway.

years.h: Washington, D.C., with [[Mouthpiece|e4a55353-84ff-4460-9d5a-1666fbe104f4]] and Give
years.p: U Street Music Hall, followed by the Glasshouse in Pomona and Chaos in Tejas.

years.h: This Is Hardcore sells out
years.p: The Philadelphia festival night is a full house. That October they open for [[Danzig|8925a01a-8608-411d-a90b-f3a52d061208]] at Riot Fest in Chicago.

years.h: Schreifels and Siegler come home
years.p: The 1988 rhythm section returns. Berlin that night, Meerhout, Belgium the next.

years.h: The Book of Revelation Records, Los Angeles
years.p: Night two at 1720 with [[Side By Side|8dc812b1-d387-4c45-8173-f0d5bd0c318f]], billed as that band's final reunion show. [[Judge|3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e]] had the night before.

years.h: Four nights in the Northeast with [[Bold|b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa]]
years.p: Pawtucket, then The Meadows in Brooklyn, the Lithuanian Music Hall in Philadelphia and Amityville Music Hall, with Swedish Revelation band Speedway on the bills. Thirty-nine years after the two bands first shared a CBGB matinee bill.
